Rotary celebrates community work and 890 Ukraine shoeboxes

4th October
Rotary Club
Charity
Basingstoke
By Kimberley Barber Regional editor

Share

1 comment

Nearly 900 shoeboxes for war-torn Ukraine, thousands of volunteer hours and major community events were among the achievements celebrated as Basingstoke Deane Rotary Club brought together charities, businesses and supporters for its annual Supporting Our Communities evening.

The volunteers, charities and community groups making a difference across Basingstoke were celebrated with an evening at Test Valley Golf Club on Tuesday, September 29.

Members and guests heard from a range of charities and community organisations while learning more about the work of Basingstoke Deane Rotary Club and the wider Rotary movement, both locally and around the world.

Rotary president Debbie McLatch opened the evening by highlighting another busy year for the club and the impact its members have had across the borough and beyond.

Rotary president Debbie McLatch at Basingstoke Deane Rotary Club's Supporting Our Communities evening at Test Valley Golf Club on Tuesday, September 29. (Image: Rod Clarke)

Among the achievements highlighted was the Christmas shoebox appeal for Ukraine, which saw the club collect an impressive 890 shoeboxes packed with gifts and essential items for families affected by the war.

Mrs McLatch also spoke about the thousands of hours volunteered by club members and the many events they help organise and support, including the popular Basingstoke Festival of Transport, which attracts thousands of visitors each year.

She outlined the club's continued support for Rotary's End Polio Now campaign, which aims to eradicate polio worldwide, as well as fundraising efforts for ShelterBox, the international disaster relief charity that provides emergency shelter and supplies to people displaced by conflict and natural disasters.

Joe Haynes and Wendy Randell, Director of Midwifery, from Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, at Basingstoke Deane Rotary Club's Supporting Our Communities evening at Test Valley Golf Club on Tuesday, September 29. (Image: Rod Clarke)

Members also heard about support for Lendwithcare, a scheme which provides small loans to entrepreneurs in developing countries, helping them start or grow businesses and improve their livelihoods.

Introducing representatives from charities and organisations the club has worked with over the past year, Mrs McLatch welcomed guests from groups including Oakley Stitchers, a community sewing group whose members create handmade items for charities and people in need, and Hampshire Hospitals Charity, which supports patients, staff and services across the county's hospitals.

She said: "Tonight is all about bringing community charities and organisations that we work with together."

Former Basingstoke mayor Colin Phillimore also addressed the gathering, while Ryan Cox, from LG Motion, spoke about the company's sponsorship of the club's activities and community work, as did Mark Jones, from Stronger Together Forum.

Martin Fielder, Club Vice President at Basingstoke Deane Rotary Club's Supporting Our Communities evening at Test Valley Golf Club on Tuesday, September 29. (Image: Rod Clarke)

Bob Evans, the club's community lead, highlighted initiatives aimed at supporting young people, including the Young Carers Festival, which gives young carers an opportunity to enjoy activities, make friends and take a break from their caring responsibilities.

The evening provided an opportunity for local organisations to share their work, strengthen partnerships and celebrate the difference volunteers make within the community.

It also served as a reminder of the many causes supported by Rotary members.

Debbie said: "Service before self - that really is our message. We are all like-minded people who connect others to achieve more together than we could apart."

For more on the club, and how to join, go to rotary-ribi.org/clubs/homepage.php?ClubID=1523
